\emph{âshpazkhâne} is built from three native pieces: \emph{âsh}, \textquotedblleft{}soup, cooked food\textquotedblright{}, \emph{-paz}, \textquotedblleft{}cooking\textquotedblright{} (the present stem of \emph{pokhtan}, \textquotedblleft{}to cook\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{khâne}, \textquotedblleft{}house\textquotedblright{}: the cook-house.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{حمام} (hammâm)}{حمام (hammâm)}]{\fa{حمام} (hammâm) — a bathroom}

\label{lesson:FA-C48-hammam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bottle, then the Persian for a kitchen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{حمام}}
\textbf{\fa{حمام}} — \emph{hammâm} — \textquotedblleft{}a bathroom\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hammâm} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{ḥammām}, \textquotedblleft{}bath, bathhouse\textquotedblright{}. Its Arabic root is \emph{ḥ-m-m} (Lane). The root is about heat: a bath was a heated room.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{cousinweb}
